headline: Guidance raised again as senior housing demand accelerates
summary_short: Revenue rose 21.7% year over year to $1,729.6M, with Normalized FFO per share up 9% to $0.97. Ventas raised its full-year 2026 investment guidance to $4.5 billion (from $3 billion) and lifted its Normalized FFO per share guidance midpoint to $3.88.
summary_long: Revenue rose 21.7% y/y to $1,729.6M, driven by the Senior Housing Operating Portfolio, where Same-Store Cash NOI grew 16% on 9% Same-Store Cash Operating Revenue growth and 210bp margin expansion; RevPOR rose 5% and occupancy grew 300bp. Net income attributable to common stockholders was $70.6M ($0.14/share, basic and diluted), while Normalized FFO per share rose 9% to $0.97 and Nareit FFO per share rose 15% to $0.99. Net Debt/Further Adjusted EBITDA improved to 4.7x from 5.6x. Cash fell 67.6% to $199.0M after funding $3.4B of year-to-date senior housing investments, partly via $2.6B of settled equity forward sales. Ventas raised full-year 2026 investment guidance to $4.5B (from $3B) and its Normalized FFO per share guidance midpoint to $3.88 (from $3.86).
confidence_notes: This is a force-regenerated run for VTR US FY2026 Q2 (Step-0 exists-guard bypassed per explicit instruction); no prior summary file existed on disk for this period, so this write is a fresh first print rather than an overwrite of prior content. Normalized FFO for both the current and prior-year quarter has been restated to exclude non-cash stock-based compensation expense, per a methodology change the company adopted beginning Q1 2026 (see footnote 1 in the FFO reconciliation) — the $0.89 2025 Normalized FFO/share figure in this release differs from what Ventas originally reported for Q2 2025. Revenue, gross profit, EBITDA, EBIT and operating income carry Yahoo fundamentals-timeseries ('wire') provenance in the shard while EPS, pretax income, cash and equity carry SEC-verbatim ('regulatory') provenance; both sets reconcile to the GAAP figures in this same press release, so there is no cross-basis inconsistency, only a provenance-tag distinction in the ledger. Full-year 2026 guidance (Attributable Net Income, Nareit FFO, and Normalized FFO per share, plus senior-housing investment volume) was written to the event's guidance[] array as 'raised' versus the April 27, 2026 guidance. Nareit FFO/share and total-company same-store cash NOI growth were extracted into extendedMetrics[] per the REIT sector KPI set; AFFO/share and an absolute occupancy % were not disclosed by name in this release (Ventas reports Normalized FFO rather than AFFO, and only occupancy deltas in basis points, not an absolute level) and were therefore omitted rather than approximated.

drivers.explanation: SHOP same-store cash operating revenue grew 9%, on RevPOR growth of 5% and average occupancy up 300 basis points year-over-year, per the release's SHOP Growth section.
Total Company NOI grew 17% year-over-year, led by SHOP performance, which lifted EBITDA even as depreciation rose.
EBIT fell despite EBITDA growth because depreciation and amortization rose 17.3% y/y to $407.7M as the real estate portfolio expanded, more than offsetting NOI gains.
Net income grew as SHOP-driven NOI gains outpaced a larger loss from unconsolidated entities ($7.8M vs $1.1M a year earlier) and higher interest expense.
EPS fell despite net income growth because weighted diluted shares rose 8.4% y/y to 497.7M, mostly from settling equity forward sales to fund investment growth; dilution outpaced earnings growth.
Cash fell as the Company funded $3.4 billion of year-to-date senior housing investments; total liquidity of $4.9 billion also includes unsettled equity forward sales and credit-facility availability.
Equity rose after Ventas settled 31.4 million shares under equity forward sales agreements for $2.6 billion of gross proceeds year to date to fund investment growth.
Diluted share count rose as the Company settled shares under equity forward sales agreements to help fund its accelerated senior housing investment pipeline.

CEO Cafaro cites strong and strengthening senior housing demand from aging baby boomers against historically low new supply, which drove this quarter's SHOP outperformance and prompted a second consecutive raise to full-year 2026 investment and per-share guidance.
